units.reproduce: Closed-book, derive l_{i,j} from softmax cross-entropy over pairwise similarities. Then compute the tau = 1 loss by hand for embeddings [1,0], [1,0], [0,1], [0,1] and get 0.5514.

selfTest.a: For row 0 the positive scores 1 and the two negatives score 0, so l = -1 + log(e + 2) = 0.5514. Rows 1, 2 and 3 match by symmetry, and the mean over all four rows is 0.5514.
selfTest.q: Embeddings [1,0], [1,0], [0,1], [0,1] at tau = 1 give loss 0.5514. Show the per-row terms.

selfTest.a: log 3 = 1.0986. Every row is uniform over its three candidates, so each row contributes log 3.
selfTest.q: All four embeddings are identical. What is the loss at tau = 1?

selfTest.a: Raw dot products mix angle with norm, so loud vectors dominate the softmax. With normalization plus temperature the loss weights examples by relative hardness, and Top-1 rises from 57.2 to 64.4 at the best setting.
selfTest.q: Why does SimCLR Table 5 favor L2 normalization?

selfTest.a: Yes. The sum runs over all k != i including the positive index j, which keeps the loss a proper cross-entropy bounded below by 0.
selfTest.q: Is the positive pair part of its own denominator?

units.title: Embedding geometry and contrastive logits
traps: Calling cosine similarity translation-invariant. It is invariant to positive scaling, not to shifts; centering the batch changes all angles.
Dropping the positive from the denominator. SimCLR sums over k != i, which includes the positive; without it the loss can go negative.
Reading NT-Xent as fixed-class classification. The classes are the current batch views, so the same pair gets a different loss in different batches.
units.why: Contrastive objectives compare directions, not positions. If norms leak into the logits, the loss rewards loud embeddings instead of aligned ones.

fit.note: Depth failed: the pool has no temperature, batch-size or positive-construction analysis. SimCLR Sections 3.1, 5.1 and 5.2 supply verified ablations beside the CLIP-loss implementation.

focus: Dividing by tau multiplies every logit gap. Small tau sharpens toward argmax; large tau flattens toward uniform.
The positive-logit gradient is -(1 - p_pos)/tau. Easy pairs saturate near zero gradient at small tau, so hard negatives drive learning.
Negatives per positive equal 2(N-1): 510 at batch 256 and 16,382 at batch 8192. Longer training closes much of the batch gap.
Random crop plus color distortion wins because it blocks the color-histogram shortcut, not because either transform is strong alone.
outcomes: Derive the 1/tau sharpening of logits and gradients, and predict saturation at small tau.
Explain how batch size sets the negative count and when longer training closes the gap.
Build positives by augmentation composition and state the invariance each transform declares.

units.reproduce: Closed-book, write the NT-Xent gradient for the positive similarity. For similarities [2, 1, 0], compute the tau = 1 softmax [0.665, 0.245, 0.090] with gradient -0.335, and the tau = 0.1 gradient of about -0.0005.

selfTest.a: e^2/(e^2 + e + 1) = 0.665. The remaining mass splits 0.245 and 0.090.
selfTest.q: Similarities [2, 1, 0] at tau = 1: what is the positive probability?

selfTest.a: The softmax saturates to one-hot, so (1 - p)/tau goes to 0 for decided pairs and learning concentrates on the remaining hard pairs; too small stalls training.
selfTest.q: What happens to easy-pair gradients as tau goes to 0?

selfTest.a: 16,382: every other view in the 2N batch except the anchor, which is 2N-2 with one positive and the rest negatives.
selfTest.q: Batch 8192 gives how many negatives per positive, and why?

selfTest.a: The task is solvable by shortcut, such as color histograms under crop-only augmentation. Composition makes pairing harder and representations better.
selfTest.q: Positive-identification accuracy is near perfect but linear evaluation is poor. What went wrong?

units.title: Temperature, negatives and positive construction
traps: Pushing tau ever lower. Below 0.1 easy pairs saturate and a few hard negatives dominate; Table 5 drops from 64.4 at 0.1 to 59.7 at 0.05.
Assuming bigger batches always win. Gains saturate near batch 8192 and longer training erases most of the gap.
Supervising positives with labels. Positive pairs come free from two views of one image; class labels never enter the loss.
units.why: Temperature and batch size set the difficulty of the discrimination game. The positive construction declares which variation the representation must ignore.
